subject: Follow-up: Benchmark download -> Deep-dive demo & reschedule request
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@fluxanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick follow-up after benchmark download

Hi Mina,

I downloaded the Redwood benchmark report earlier today (great write-up, thanks). I tried to book a demo via the calendar link on the results page but I think I accidentally picked the wrong timezone and the slot conflicts with our sprint planning.

We're a small infra/ML team evaluating inference options and would like a longer, 60-minute deep-dive rather than a quick intro — specifically to cover end-to-end latency for tail requests, quantization trade-offs for our LLMs, and an estimate of cost per inference at our scale. I'll likely bring a colleague, Sara Kim (cc'ed here), who owns the infra side.

Can you help reschedule to a 60-minute slot? Our preferred windows are the mornings (ET) of Mar 2 or Mar 3.

Also, the benchmark referenced our dataset (FluxBench) — if you have a PDF copy you can share ahead of the call, that'd be helpful.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Senior ML Engineer
Flux Analytics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fluxanalytics.com>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fluxanalytics.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after benchmark download

Thanks for downloading the report and for the context, Liam — great to meet you (virtually). I can absolutely set up a 60-minute deep-dive and will include Dev on the invite to cover serving/infra details.

Attached: benchmark-report-fluxanalytics-20270220.pdf (excerpt with the charts you saw) and a quick mutual action plan (redwood-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) to keep the call focused.

Are mornings ET on Mar 2 or Mar 3 still good? If you prefer, here are two specific options I can hold:
- Tue, Mar 2, 10:00–11:00 AM ET
- Wed, Mar 3, 10:00–11:00 AM ET

If either works, I will send a Google Calendar invite and include the agenda: 1) workload profile & target SLOs, 2) latency tail behavior and batching strategies, 3) quantization/accuracy trade-offs, 4) pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted options, 5) next steps & M.A.P.

Also linking the HubSpot record so our CSM can prep: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/fluxanalytics

—Mina
Mina Haddad
SDR, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@fluxanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fluxanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-02-22T09:48:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after benchmark download

Hi Mina — thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the materials. I reviewed the excerpt and the M.A.P. looks sensible.

Small update: we have an all-hands on Tue morning (Mar 2) so that slot won't work. Can we lock Wed, Mar 3 — preferably 10:00–11:00 AM ET as you suggested? Also, please include whoever handles pricing/commit options on your side (we've got some questions about Reserved vs Pay-as-you-go at our expected volume).

One more ask: would it be possible to get a short (1–2 slide) summary of expected cost ranges for 10k, 100k, and 1M inference tokens per month? It'll help our procurement folks.

Thanks — Liam
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fluxanalytics.com>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fluxanalytics.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-22T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after benchmark download

Perfect — I've booked Wed, Mar 3, 10:00–11:00 AM ET and sent a calendar invite (Google Calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123def456). Invite includes the agenda I outlined and the two attachments from earlier.

Dev will cover runtime/throughput and tail latency strategies, and Lauren (cc'd) will join to cover commercial/commit options. I'll bring a brief cost-range slide for the 10k / 100k / 1M token buckets. If you have any sample traffic characteristics or an expected QPS, send them along and we can tailor the walkthrough.

Looking forward to it — I'll follow up with the invite and prep notes.

Best,
Mina Haddad
SDR, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-mutual-action-plan.xlsx, benchmark-report-fluxanalytics-20270220.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@fluxanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-02-25T14:20:00-05:00
Subject: Quick note before the Mar 3 deep-dive

Mina / Dev / Liam — looping in a quick checklist from my side so the deep-dive is operationally useful: 
- Please confirm expected model sizes (approx. params) and typical sequence lengths for the demo.
- If Flux has PII constraints, confirm whether the data will be shared in production (affects Private vs Hosted discussion).
- I'll bring the Reserved capacity tiers and a one-slide comparison of SLA differences.

Liam — if you can reply to this thread with the model names/sizes and an estimated monthly token count, we'll make sure the deck covers your procurement questions.

Thanks — Lauren Bishop
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
